scenarios.title: The Late-Night Show
scenarios.text: A late-night show wants you as a guest during the bye week. The producers want a funny kicker story and maybe a kick on the studio set.

choices.label: Be funny
choices.result: You're funny, mostly at your own expense. The clip goes around the league, and the whole locker room does the bit back at you for a month.

choices.label: Bring one story
choices.result: You bring one good story about your first pro camp and tell it well. The host stops laughing long enough to say it was a good story.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline and spend the bye week at home. The producers book a punter instead, and he's better on television than you'd have been.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Field
scenarios.text: Your hometown is naming the youth field after you, the one with the crooked goalpost where you learned to kick. The ceremony is in June.

choices.label: Bring the family
choices.result: You bring the whole family. {parent} stands under the sign for a long time without saying anything, then asks someone to take the picture again.

choices.label: Kick the first ball
choices.result: You kick the first ball with the youth league. It hits the crooked post, the kids scream, and it's the best thing that happens all summer.

choices.label: Keep it quiet
choices.result: You ask them to keep it small: no speeches, just the sign. Afterward you walk the field alone and find your old spot by the fence.

scenarios.title: The High School Visit
scenarios.text: You visit your old high school, and the kicking net is still behind the bleachers.

choices.label: Kick with the team
choices.result: You kick with the team. The kicker can't believe it.

choices.label: Find your old coach
choices.result: You find your old coach in the weight room.

choices.label: Stand by the net
choices.result: You stand by the net for a while.

scenarios.title: The Kicker You Mentored
scenarios.text: A kicker you spent two summers mentoring signs with a rival club, the one you play twice a year. He sends you a picture of his new locker.

choices.label: Congratulate him
choices.result: You congratulate him first, before the news breaks. He tells a reporter he learned everything from you, and you pretend not to be moved.

choices.label: Raise your game
choices.result: You raise your game. Twice a year you'll be on the same field, and you're not letting him outkick his teacher.

choices.label: Watch him play
choices.result: You watch his first game from your couch and smile at every warmup kick that looks like yours.

scenarios.title: The New Special Teams Unit
scenarios.text: Half your special teams unit is new this season: a new snapper, two new wings, a holder who has never held in a real game. The timing is all wrong.

choices.label: Teach the new ones
choices.result: You teach the new ones everything you know, from the cadence to the jokes. By October the unit sounds like a unit.

choices.label: Build the unit
choices.result: You take the unit to dinner every Thursday. The timing comes after the trust, which is how it always works.

choices.label: Rep it out
choices.result: You rep it out after every practice until the timing is right. Your leg is tired, and the operation is clean.

scenarios.title: The Coordinator's Trick Plays
scenarios.text: The coordinator wants more fakes and more onside kicks, and he wants you to run them.

choices.label: Master them
choices.result: You master every trick play. The coordinator starts calling you his secret weapon.

choices.label: Pick the best ones
choices.result: You help him pick the best three and talk him out of the rest. He thanks you later.

choices.label: Get the unit excited
choices.result: You get the unit excited. Practice is fun again.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Day Off
scenarios.text: The club gives veterans a day off each week, and you're now one of them.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result: You use the day off. Your legs thank you.

choices.label: Train anyway
choices.result: You come in anyway. Old habits. The young players notice, for better and worse.

choices.label: Spend it at home
choices.result: You spend it at home: school runs, dinner, a nap on the couch.

scenarios.title: The Body Maintenance Plan
scenarios.text: A trainer builds you a maintenance plan for the next five years.

choices.label: Follow it
choices.result: You follow it to the letter. It's dull, and your leg feels five years younger.

choices.label: Add to it
choices.result: You add your own work on top. You're stronger and more tired.

choices.label: Do half
choices.result: You do half and keep the rest of your life.

scenarios.title: The Massage Therapist
scenarios.text: The team's massage therapist has worked on your legs for years and can tell how your week went by touching your hamstring. They want you to change something.

choices.label: Listen to them
choices.result: You listen to them about everything: sleep, stretching, the way you sit on the plane. Your legs feel younger by midseason.

choices.label: Thank them
choices.result: You thank them publicly at the end of the season, in front of the whole team. They pretend to be annoyed and keep the clip.

choices.label: Book extra sessions
choices.result: You book extra sessions and sleep better than you have in years. Your bank account notices, and your legs are worth it.

scenarios.title: The Old Injury Flares
scenarios.text: An old injury flares up during a road trip.

choices.label: Tell the trainers
choices.result: You tell the trainers right away. They catch it before it gets worse.

choices.label: Work through it
choices.result: You work through it and tell them later.

choices.label: Rest it
choices.result: You rest it all week and miss the extra work. It calms down.

scenarios.title: The Long Practice Week
scenarios.text: A long week of practice in the heat, and your legs feel every year.

choices.label: Pace yourself
choices.result: You pace yourself and save your legs for Sunday.

choices.label: Push through
choices.result: You push through every rep. Your legs feel it all weekend.

choices.label: Keep the unit laughing
choices.result: You keep the unit laughing through the heat.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Retirement Speech
scenarios.text: A teammate's retirement speech mentions you by name.

choices.label: Hug him afterward
choices.result: You hug him afterward. Neither of you says much.

choices.label: Say something back
choices.result: You say something back at the team dinner.

choices.label: Keep it with you
choices.result: You keep it with you. Some nights you think about it before you sleep.

scenarios.title: The Team Historian
scenarios.text: The club's historian wants an hour with you for the team archive. She has a recorder, a list of questions and a photo of you as a rookie.

choices.label: Tell every story
choices.result: You tell every story you can remember, including some you probably shouldn't. She laughs until she has to stop the recorder.

choices.label: Tell the true ones
choices.result: You tell the true ones, carefully, including the hard years. She says it's the most honest interview in the archive.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: You keep it short. The archive gets a few good lines, and you realize later you didn't mention the people who got you there.
